title: Newborn Circumcision Care: A Pediatrician's Guide
summary: Newborn circumcision care: how to clean, use petroleum jelly, spot normal healing, and know the red flags. Talk to a Blueberry pediatrician.
body_markdown:
To care for a newborn circumcision, gently clean the tip with warm water at each diaper change. Dab a little petroleum jelly on the tip so it does not stick to the diaper. Fasten diapers loosely. Most circumcisions heal in about 7 to 10 days. Call your pediatrician right away for redness that spreads, pus, or a fever of 100.4°F (38°C) or higher. Also call for bleeding that is more than a few drops or will not stop with gentle pressure, or no wet diaper within 6 to 8 hours. This guide walks you through each day of healing, what is normal, and the signs that mean it is time to call.


## Key Takeaways


- Clean the tip with warm water at each diaper change, then dab on a little petroleum jelly.
- Fasten diapers loosely and give sponge baths only for now.
- A yellow or whitish film on the tip by day 2 or 3 is normal healing, not pus.
- The tip often looks most dramatic on days 2 to 4 - puffy, red or purple, sometimes bruised. That is normal.
- Redness or swelling that gets worse after day 3 to 5 is a reason to call the doctor.
- Most circumcisions heal in about 7 to 10 days.
- Call right away for a fever of 100.4°F or higher, bleeding that is more than a few drops or will not stop, no wet diaper in 6 to 8 hours, or a tip that looks dark blue or black.


## How do you care for a newborn circumcision?


Newborn circumcision care is simple: keep the area clean, keep it from sticking, and watch for a short list of warning signs. You do not need special soaps, wipes, or ointments beyond plain petroleum jelly. The goal is not to speed up healing - that happens on its own - but to keep the area clean and comfortable while it heals.


### The first 24 hours


Right after the procedure, the tip of the penis will look red and a little swollen. This is normal. You may see a small amount of blood - a few drops - on the diaper. A drop or two of oozing is expected in the first day.


Some babies have a Gomco or Mogen circumcision. These methods use a small clamp and leave no plastic ring. With these, there is often a gauze dressing with petroleum jelly. Remove it if it has not fallen off after about 24 hours. If it sticks, soften it first with a warm, wet washcloth. Never pull a dry dressing off. It usually falls off with the first diaper change and that is not a problem.


### Cleaning the area at each diaper change


Clean the tip gently with plain warm water at each diaper change and after every stool. You do not need soap. Let it air-dry or pat it dry softly. Do not scrub, and do not try to wipe off any yellow film you see (more on that below).


Sponge baths only for now


Skip tub baths and do not submerge your baby in water yet. For most newborns the umbilical cord stump is the deciding factor - stick to sponge baths until the stump falls off, usually 1 to 2 weeks, which is normally after the circumcision has healed. See our guides to[umbilical cord care](https://www.blueberrypediatrics.com/health-tips/newborn-umbilical-cord-care) and[how often to bathe a newborn](https://www.blueberrypediatrics.com/health-tips/a-pediatricians-guide-how-often-should-you-bathe-a-newborn) .


### Petroleum jelly and which method your baby had (Gomco/Mogen vs. Plastibell)


One of the most common questions parents ask is whether to use petroleum jelly (Vaseline) - and the answer depends on the method. Both answers are correct, for different procedures. Here is how to tell which one your baby had: look for a plastic ring on the tip. If there is a ring, it was a Plastibell. If there is no ring, it was a Gomco or Mogen.


Care step Gomco / Mogen (no ring) Plastibell (plastic ring)


Initial dressing Gauze with petroleum jelly; remove after about 24 hours if it is still on. If stuck, soften with a warm wet washcloth. No gauze dressing.


Cleaning Warm water, gently, twice a day and after each stool. Warm water, gently, twice a day and after each stool.


Petroleum jelly Yes - on the incision line and tip after each cleaning for the first 4 days. It keeps the diaper from sticking and eases discomfort. Only if your pediatrician tells you to. Do not routinely pack ointment around the ring.


The ring Not applicable. Let it fall off on its own (usually 5 to 10 days). Never pull it - pulling causes bleeding. It may hang by a thread of tissue for a day or two first; that is normal.


Healing marker The scab at the incision line separates in about 7 to 10 days. The ring falls off, then the tip finishes healing.


### Diapering and dressing


Fasten diapers loosely so nothing presses on the tip. A loose diaper cuts down on rubbing and lets air reach the area. Change diapers often to keep the area clean and dry. Frequent changes also help prevent[diaper rash](https://www.blueberrypediatrics.com/health-tips/types-of-diaper-rash) . Position the penis so it points down or toward the belly, whichever keeps it away from the diaper seam.


## What are the normal circumcision healing stages?


Normal healing looks a little alarming before it looks better - but the change to watch is direction, not just appearance. Around days 2 to 4 the tip often looks its most dramatic: puffy, deep red or purple, sometimes bruised, with a yellow or whitish film forming over it. That appearance is normal. What should not happen is getting worse: tenderness should be easing by about day 3, and redness that spreads or deepens after days 3 to 5 is a reason to call.


By about day 2 or 3 you will usually see a yellow or whitish film over the tip. This is the single thing parents most often mistake for pus. It isn't. It is part of normal healing, and unlike pus it does not wipe away and does not smell. The AAP notes it is normal to see a little yellow coating in the first week. Tell your pediatrician if it is still there after a week.


> "One of the most common circumcision worries I see on Blueberry visits is a parent certain the normal yellow film is an infection, it almost never is."
>
>
> Dr. Melissa Tribuzio, MD, Board-Certified Pediatrician


Mild swelling and bruising are also normal and fade over the first week. As the AAP puts it, the redness and secretion disappear gradually within about a week.


## What does an infected circumcision look like?


Most of what looks worrying is normal healing. The table below sorts the normal signs from the ones that mean you should call your pediatrician.


Normal healing Call the doctor


A yellow or whitish film on the tip that does not smell and does not wipe away Thick, foul-smelling yellow or green discharge (this is different from the thin yellow film)


Redness right at the tip in the first few days Redness that spreads, deepens, or streaks up the shaft after day 3 to 5


Mild swelling and bruising that ease over the first week Swelling that keeps getting larger after day 3, or severe swelling


A few drops of blood on the diaper in the first day Bleeding more than a few drops, or any bleeding that will not stop with gentle pressure


Tenderness that eases by about day 3 A tip that looks dark blue or black


Fewer wet diapers right after the procedure, then normal No wet diaper within 6 to 8 hours, or only dribbling


## How do I manage my baby's pain after circumcision?


Circumcision discomfort is usually mild and eases within about 3 to 4 days. The tenderness should be much less by day 3. Start with the comfort measures that every source agrees on before reaching for any medicine.


The simplest measure is a thin layer of petroleum jelly on the incision line - it protects the area and eases discomfort. Extra cuddling, swaddling, and feeding also comfort your baby.


Whether to give infant acetaminophen (Tylenol), and at what weight-based dose, is a decision for your pediatrician. Guidance genuinely differs on this, so do not give it on your own. Ask first.


Two firm rules about pain medicine


Never give ibuprofen to a newborn - it is not safe under 6 months. And never give any fever or pain medicine to a baby under 12 weeks who feels feverish before a doctor has seen them. That medicine can mask a fever that needs urgent care.


## When should I call the doctor about my baby's circumcision?


Most healing is uneventful. But a short list of signs needs prompt attention. Some can be reviewed by your pediatrician; a few need to be seen in person right away.


Call your pediatrician or seek care now for any of these


The tip looks dark blue or black (a sign blood flow is blocked). Severe swelling of the penis. Bleeding that is more than a few drops or will not stop after a few minutes of gentle pressure. A fever of 100.4°F (38°C) or higher - in a newborn, a fever alone is a reason to seek care urgently. No wet diaper within 6 to 8 hours, or only dribbling (swelling can block urine flow). Redness that spreads or streaks up the shaft. Pus or thick, foul-smelling discharge. A foul smell from the area. A Plastibell ring still on after 10 days, that has slipped onto the shaft, or that comes off before day 3. Any baby under 1 month who looks or acts unwell in any way, or who cannot be consoled for more than 2 hours after you have tried the comfort measures above.


A quick note on the difference between calling and going in. A telehealth visit is great for triage and the milder questions - like whether the yellow film is normal. But a fever of 100.4°F or higher in a newborn, bleeding that will not stop, no urination, or a dark or blue tip all need prompt in-person or urgent care. A photo can answer "is this normal?" It cannot take the place of a hands-on exam for those signs.


## How long does a newborn circumcision take to heal?


Most circumcisions heal in about 7 to 10 days. The AAP states the penis should be fully healed in about 1 week to 10 days after circumcision. For a Plastibell, the ring usually falls off on its own in about 5 to 10 days, and the tip finishes healing after that. For a Gomco or Mogen, the scab at the incision line separates in about 7 to 10 days.


> "The penis should be fully healed in about 1 week to 10 days after circumcision."
>
>
> American Academy of Pediatrics


Healing cannot safely be sped up - it is physical. The best thing you can do is keep the area clean and comfortable and know what normal healing looks like.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### Is a yellow film on the tip normal?


Yes. By day 2 or 3 you will usually see a yellow or whitish film over the tip. It is normal healing, not pus. Unlike pus, it does not wipe away and does not smell. Tell your pediatrician if it is still there after a week.


### Do I use petroleum jelly, and does it depend on the method?


It depends. For a Gomco or Mogen circumcision (no ring), yes. Apply a little petroleum jelly to the incision line and tip after each cleaning for the first 4 days. For a Plastibell (with a ring), use it only if your pediatrician tells you to.


### Why does it look worse before it looks better?


Around days 2 to 4 the tip often looks its most dramatic - puffy, red or purple, sometimes bruised, with a yellow film. That appearance is normal. The part to watch is direction: tenderness should ease by about day 3, and redness that spreads after day 3 to 5 is a reason to call.


### When can I give my baby a bath?


Give sponge baths only for now. For most newborns the umbilical cord stump is the deciding factor - wait until the stump falls off, usually 1 to 2 weeks, before a tub bath. That is normally after the circumcision has healed.


### What if the Plastibell ring hasn't fallen off?


It usually falls off on its own in about 5 to 10 days. Never pull it. Call your pediatrician if the ring is still on after 10 days, has slipped onto the shaft, or comes off before day 3.
